overview.description: Earl of Coventry is a classic English 'Stops' or matching round game, closely related to Snip Snap Snorum. Unlike many complex card games, it is defined by its rhythmic verbal component - players recite rhyming phrases as they match the ranks played by their opponents. The game is a fast-paced shedding contest where the primary goal is to reach the 'stop' card (the fourth card of a rank) to regain control of the lead. Historically popular as a Victorian-era parlor game, it remains a charming social exercise in rhythm and rank tracking.

history.origins: Originating in 18th-century England, it is part of a broad family of 'rhyming games' that were common before the rise of trick-taking dominance. The name refers to the Earl of Coventry, though whether it honors a specific historical figure or simply used the name for its phonetic fit in the rhyme is debated.
timeline: 1700s: Early forms of Snip Snap Snorum documented in English clubs.
1800s: Becomes a popular 'round game' for children and mixed social groups.
Modern: Survives primarily as a historical curiosity and children's card game.
history.evolution: Evolution from a gambling 'stop' game to a social 'rhyme' game for all ages.
history.cultural: Used in the 19th century as a social icebreaker, where the emphasis was as much on the spirited recitation of the rhyme as it was on the card play.

setup.players: 4 to 8 players; best with a larger group to ensure cards are widely distributed.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out one by one. It does not matter if some players have one card more than others.

rules.objective: Be the first player to shed all cards from your hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: The player to the dealer's left plays any card from their hand. For example, a 5.
2. Matching: The next player must play a 5 if they have one. Each subsequent player must match that rank.
3. The Rhyme: With each card played, the player MUST say the corresponding line:
   - 1st Card: 'There's as good as 5 can be.'
   - 2nd Card: 'There's a 5 as good as he.'
   - 3rd Card: 'There's the best of all the three.'
   - 4th Card: 'And there's the Earl of Coventry!'
4. Re-Lead: The person who plays the 4th card of the rank (the Earl) immediately leads any card they wish to start the next sequence.
keyRules: If you do not have a card of the rank currently being played, you pass your turn.
If NO ONE can play the next card in the sequence (e.g., the remaining 3s have already been played earlier), the last person to play a card of that rank leads a new card.
Verbal accuracy is traditionally required; failure to say the rhyme correctly may result in a small penalty in home rules.

strategy.basic: Prioritize leading ranks of which you hold multiple cards. If you hold three of a kind, you can almost guarantee being the one to play the 'best of all the three,' but you'll need the 4th player to enable you or wait for someone else to lead the 4th.
strategy.intermediate: Leading Pairs: Leading from a pair is safe, as it allows you to maintain some control over when that rank is exhausted.
strategy.advanced: Stop Tracking: Keep track of which ranks have already had their 4th card ('the Earl') played. Once a 4th card is played, that rank is 'dead'. Use this knowledge to determine which other ranks are likely to be playable.
tips: If you hold the 4th card of a rank (the Earl), you have 'The Stop'. Save it for when you need to regain the lead to play your own advantageous sequences.
Don't lead a single card if you hold the other three; you are giving 'The Earl' (the lead) to an opponent.

difficulty.easy: Leads cards randomly; doesn't track which ranks are dead.
difficulty.medium: Conserves 'Earl' cards to regain the lead; leads from large sets to maximize control.
difficulty.hard: Simulates hand distributions based on who passed on which ranks; perfect memory of all dead ranks.

considerations: AI must prioritize moves that result in playing the 4th card, as the lead is the most powerful resource in the game.

pass.description: Pass your turn when you do not hold a card of the rank currently being played.
pass.constraints: Legal only when you cannot match the current rank. Play passes clockwise to next player.

engine.handRankingSystem: No hand ranking; first player to empty their hand wins.
engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card deck consisting of fifty-two cards in four suits, with thirteen ranks per suit from Ace low to King high; the entire deck is dealt out and no jokers are used.
engine.suitDescription: French suit set: four suits—Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs—each with thirteen cards, using the standard international symbols (♠ ♥ ♦ ♣).
engine.rankDescription: Standard fifty-two rank set: Ace (low), 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King (high), with thirteen cards in each suit; Aces are low in this game.
engine.dealPattern: One card at a time clockwise to each player until deck is empty; unequal hand sizes allowed.
